author: Stefan Bogdanescu

content: # Undefined property: Illuminate\Pagination\LengthAwarePaginator::$name When paginating data in Laravel, developers often encounter a confusing error message if they mix up the pagination wrapper object with the actual collection of items. The specific error `Undefined property: Illuminate\Pagination\LengthAwarePaginator::$name` is a classic symptom of a scope confusion within Blade templates. It happens because the code attempts to access properties on the paginator instance itself rather than on the records inside it. In the scenario provided, the controller executes a standard query using `DB::table('birlikte_calisalim')->paginate(15)`. This returns an instance of `Illuminate\Pagination\LengthAwarePaginator` (or `Paginator`). When this object is passed to the view via `compact(['users'])`, the variable `$users` holds the paginator wrapper, not the raw collection. The error manifests in the view when the loop iterates incorrectly or when properties are accessed on the wrong level. Look closely at this snippet from the provided view: ```blade @foreach($users as $row) {{$users->name}} {{$users->email}} {{$users->tarih}} {{$users->message}} @endforeach ``` The fatal mistake lies in the loop logic. The `@foreach($users as $row)` directive correctly iterates over the items in the collection, assigning each user record to the variable `$row`. However, immediately inside the loop, the code attempts to access `$users->name`, `$users->email`, and so on. Here is the technical breakdown of why this fails: 1. **$users** refers to the `LengthAwarePaginator` object. This object contains metadata like total counts, links for previous/next pages, and the underlying collection. It does not possess properties like `name`, `email`, or `tarih`. Those columns belong to the database rows. 2. Inside the loop, **$row** refers to the individual database record (an array-like object or Eloquent model). This is where the `name`, `email`, and `tarih` properties actually exist. By referencing `$users` inside the loop, you are trying to read the `name` property of the paginator wrapper itself. Since `LengthAwarePaginator` does not define a `name` property, PHP throws the `Undefined property` error. Even if it didn't throw an error immediately, it would render the same row with identical data for every single iteration because `$users` never changes during the loop. ### The Fix: Accessing the Correct Scope To resolve this, you must access the properties of the variable currently in scope (`$row`) rather than the wrapper (`$users`). Update the Blade template as follows: ```blade @foreach($users as $user) {{ $user->name }} {{ $user->email }} {{ $user->tarih }} {{ $user->message }} @endforeach ``` Note the change from `$users` to `$user` (or keeping `$row`) and accessing the properties on that specific variable. Additionally, ensure your database table `birlikte_calisalim` has columns matching these property names exactly, including case sensitivity if using Eloquent model mapping. If you are using raw arrays from `DB::table`, ensure the keys match; otherwise, use a Model relationship to define the correct accessor names. ### Handling Pagination Links The pagination links (`{{ $users->links() }}`) should remain outside the loop. The paginator object retains its state (current page, total pages) throughout the view lifecycle. Placing `links()` inside the loop would result in rendering the pagination controls multiple times, once per row. Keep the link generator at the bottom of the table structure to ensure it appears only once, typically below the `` or after the closing `` tag depending on your layout requirements. ### Summary of Common Pitfalls This specific error is frequently caused by one of two habits: 1. **Naming Confusion**: Using `$users` for both the paginator and a collection variable in different contexts, leading to ambiguity about which object holds the data. 2. **Assumption of Model Structure**: Assuming that because the previous project worked, the current setup must be identical without verifying that the property access paths match the current scope. If you are looking for additional resources on Laravel pagination best practices or need to troubleshoot similar wrapper vs. collection issues, reviewing guides from [LaravelCompany](https://laravelcompany.com) can provide further context on handling paginated data structures efficiently.
